absent: No locking discipline, concurrency rules or synchronization objects appear in these fragments.
No callable entry points, function bodies or implementation behaviour beyond header layouts and numeric ABI are shown.
No validation limits, error handling policy, timer values or protocol state transitions beyond notification discriminants are defined here.
No boot, capability, microVM, game state, rollback, Computer Use or commit frontier semantics are described by these headers.

findings.text: The traffic control action header is a compact fixed header whose leading octet carries address family and whose remaining octets are reserved padding. Consumers locate trailing attributes by aligning this header size inside the enclosing netlink message and derive remaining payload length from the netlink header. Root attributes for this family form a tiny zero based set covering table selection with an action alias, plus flags, object count, millisecond delta and extended warning, with public maximum one below an internal sentinel.

Routing netlink multicast groups form a zero based dense numbering where RTNLGRP_NONE means no subscription and later values identify link, neighbour, traffic control, address, route, rule, prefix, discovery option, bridge, tunnel, statistics and family specific topics. The sequence holds reserved no operation slots, ends with an internal maximum sentinel, defines RTNLGRP_MAX as one below it, and mirrors each enumerator with a same named preprocessor symbol.

Dump control uses low single bit flags where the lowest bit requests large dumps and another low bit requests terse action dumps, with an action alias for the large dump bit. Extended information filtering uses distinct low bit masks spanning nine bit positions to select virtual function data, bridge VLAN data including a compressed form, statistics skipping, subsystem detail groups and a name only mode.

The boot video setup record named screen_info is a packed fixed layout of roughly five dozen octets. It preserves text mode cursor coordinates, extended memory, video page, mode, columns, lines and related firmware values at stable low offsets, then describes a linear frame buffer by width, height, depth, base, size, line length, colour component sizes and positions, protected mode entry, page count, attributes, capability word, extended base high half and reserved tail.

Display type codes use small hexadecimal discriminants to distinguish monochrome text, CGA, monochrome and colour EGA, colour VGA, VESA graphics, platform frame buffers and EFI graphics, including VIDEO_TYPE_VGAC for colour VGA and VIDEO_TYPE_EFI for EFI graphics. One flag bit marks absence of cursor and capability bits record skipping of quirks and interpretation of the base as a sixty four bit value.

Each user visible header carries a single include guard macro ensuring one time inclusion. The guard has no runtime meaning and only prevents repeated definition when headers are included multiple times.

Association identity named sctp_assoc_t is a signed thirty two bit integer. Three small scope discriminants select future associations with value zero, the current association with value one, or all associations with value two.

Primary socket options occupy a dense zero based numeric range through the thirties, starting with SCTP_RTOINFO at zero and continuing through association, initiation, delay, close, primary address, adaptation, fragmentation, peer parameters, default send, events, mapped addresses, segment size, status, peer information, acknowledgement timing with two aliases, context, interleaving, delivery point, burst, authentication management, association enumeration, thresholds, receive info toggles, default info, key control, port reuse and an extended threshold variant.

Extended operations use numbers around one hundred, including bind addition and removal, peel off with a flags variant, legacy and current connect variants, peer and local address listing, statistics, partial reliability support and status, reconfiguration support, reset enablement and execution, stream addition, scheduler selection and value, interleaving support, connected send, generic event control, feature probes, failed state exposure with an alias, encapsulation port and probe interval. SCTP_GET_PEER_ADDRS and SCTP_GET_LOCAL_ADDRS denote address listing operations.

Partial reliability policy occupies two middle bits of a flag word, with distinct values for none, time constrained, retransmission constrained and priority handling, plus a mask and a maximum alias. Helpers extract the policy from flags, install a policy into flags, test whether each mode is enabled, and convert a policy token into a zero based table index.

Reconfiguration enablement uses three low bits for stream reset requests, association reset requests and association change requests with a combined mask. Stream reset direction uses separate low bits distinguishing incoming from outgoing streams.

Ancillary message kinds form a zero based enumeration distinguishing initiation, combined send receive header, separate send and receive descriptors, next message preview, partial reliability descriptor, authentication descriptor and destination address for both address families, each mirrored by a same named macro. Send and receive flags use low bits for unordered delivery, address override, abort, immediate acknowledgement and broadcast style behaviours, while MSG_NOTIFICATION marks notifications using a high bit and end of stream reuses the generic finish indication.

Initiation parameters consist of four sixteen bit counts for outbound streams, inbound streams, attempts and timeout. Combined send receive information carries stream identity, sequence values, flags, payload protocol identifier, context, lifetime, transmission numbers and association identity. The split send descriptor carries a shorter subset with stream, flags, protocol identifier, context and association identity.

Receive side descriptors share a pattern of stream identity, flags, protocol identifier and association identity, with the current message view adding sequence, transmission and cumulative transmission numbers plus context, and the next message preview adding a length field instead. Partial reliability parameters pair a sixteen bit policy with a thirty two bit value, authentication parameters carry only a sixteen bit key number, and a small union conveys either a raw octet, initiation parameters or combined send receive information as ancillary data.

Association change notifications carry a common type, flags and length prefix followed by state, error, outbound and inbound stream counts, association identity and trailing variable bytes. Peer address change notifications carry the same prefix plus a socket address storage field, integer state and error, and association identity, with packed four octet alignment. Remote error notifications carry the same prefix plus a big endian error code, association identity and trailing variable bytes.

Association state cycles through communication up, communication lost, restart, shutdown complete and refusal to start a new association. Peer address state cycles through available, unreachable, removed, added, made primary, confirmed and potentially failed with a short alias for the failed state. Send outcome distinguishes data never sent from data already sent.

Failed send notifications share a prefix of type, flags, length and error, then embed either combined or split send information, plus association identity and trailing unsent bytes. Shutdown, adaptation and partial delivery notifications reuse the same prefix pattern with association identity, adding respectively no extra state, an adaptation indication, or an indication plus stream and sequence values. Partial delivery defines an abort indication value of zero.

Authentication key notifications carry type, flags, length, current and alternate key numbers, an indication and association identity, with states for new key including a compatibility alias, freed key and missing authentication. Sender dry, stream reset, association reset and stream change notifications all share the same type, flags, length and association identity prefix, adding respectively no payload, a variable stream list, local and remote transmission numbers, or inbound and outbound stream counts with denied and failed flag bits. A subscription record holds one octet toggle per event class, and a top level union overlays a generic header with every concrete notification body.

Several layouts need careful bounds handling: the video setup and address change records use packed representation with explicit offsets and alignment, and association change, remote error, failed send and stream reset bodies end with flexible trailing byte or stream arrays whose extent is governed only by the length prefix.

Every notification body begins with the same three field header of sixteen bit type, sixteen bit flags and thirty two bit length, allowing generic dispatch before interpreting the remaining fields. Enumerated option, group, message and state values are stable user visible ABI and several historic names are preserved as aliases rather than removed.
